correctness.rationale: For all k>=4 the Perron cubic has positive root below one, giving convergence of the Katz resolvent. Four exact walk-score equations separate every Katz maximizer to the two high-gain loop vertices. Upper-capped trajectories from those vertices cannot give more than 2+(k+1)epsilon total per time, while seed b reaches k leaves at t=1; the claimed all-k ratio follows. The finite exact-fraction checker is auxiliary only.

value.rationale: This is an explicit, all-size impossibility for uniform approximation by the source-paper linear-optimal Katz initial seed in nonlinear capped GIP. It isolates saturation/feedback rather than positive adoption threshold or disconnectedness, and shows why linear walk prominence can disagree arbitrarily with nonlinear seed utility. The absence of any positive worst-case ratio is a meaningful qualitative benchmark for heuristic design.
